source_families: Australian Bureau of Statistics General Social Survey

records.geography: Australia; people aged 15 years and over for cultural participation and people aged 18 years and over for social experiences, with all-household financial-stress measures

cash_flow_problem_2020.unit: percent of households reporting at least one cash-flow problem in the previous 12 months

cash_flow_problem_2025.unit: percent of households reporting at least one cash-flow problem in the previous 12 months

dissaving_2020.unit: percent of households reporting at least one dissaving action in the previous 12 months

dissaving_2025.unit: percent of households reporting at least one dissaving action in the previous 12 months

outside_household_weekly_contact_2020.unit: percent of adults with weekly face-to-face contact with family or friends outside the household in the previous three months

outside_household_weekly_contact_2025.unit: percent of adults with weekly face-to-face contact with family or friends outside the household in the previous three months

records.geography: Australia; weekly national consumer-confidence survey, with state-level movement reported

better_off_now.unit: percent saying their family is better off financially than a year ago, down 2 percentage points

worse_off_now.unit: percent saying their family is worse off financially than a year ago

buying_intention.value: 16% said it was a good time to buy major household items, while 44% said it was a bad time

blocking_items: ABS measures are 2020-to-2025 repeated cross-sections while ANZ/Roy Morgan is a weekly 2026 release
household financial-stress, adult social-contact, and confidence-index denominators differ
no common holdout period or outcome definition
publisher methods and sampling frames differ
next_action: Acquire an independent repeated household-finance or purchase-behavior series with a compatible population and period before promoting the candidate.
boundary: Independent publishers can challenge the household-room mechanism without making unlike measures numerically comparable.
